title: Municipal Urban Microgrid Policy Research Brief
prompt: Write a 2-page executive research brief advising a mid-sized city council on whether to fund two municipal solar-plus-storage microgrids for emergency resilience (hospital + community shelter). Synthesize the provided empirical evidence, compare financing options (municipal green bond vs. third-party PPA vs. federal grant co-funding), identify interconnection and permitting risks, and deliver an 18-month phased recommendation with measurable KPIs.
materials:
Source Packet:
1. Bronzeville Community Microgrid (Chicago, IL): 7 MW peak, cut critical-facility outage hours by 71% over 3 years; 4-hour battery islanding; interconnection review took 11 months.
2. Redwood Coast Airport Microgrid (Humboldt, CA): 2.2 MW solar + 9 MWh battery, capex $5.4M, offset 32% by state resilience grant; reduced diesel backup runtime by 68%.
3. Municipal Finance Memo: City has $4.0M capital reserve, AA- bond rating (4.6% yield, 15-year term), and faces a strict 18-month grant expenditure deadline.
4. Utility Tariff Note: Standby demand charges add ~$110k/yr unless islanding sites enroll in peak-shaving demand response.
mid_task_requirement: Mid-task council directive (inject at ~50% progress): The Mayor's Office requires that at least 40% of project benefits and emergency backup capacity explicitly serve low-income neighborhoods, and capped municipal cash outlay at $2.5M (no general-fund borrowing above that cap). Do NOT alter the already-verified Empirical Evidence section.
rubric_criteria: Accuracy & grounding in source packet figures (0-2 pts)
Rigorous comparison of financing & regulatory trade-offs (0-2 pts)
Full integration of 40% low-income equity rule & $2.5M cash cap (0-2 pts)
Preservation of accurate empirical evidence without contradictions (0-2 pts)
Clarity, executive structure, and concrete 18-month KPIs (0-2 pts)

title: Annual Civic Tech Summit Event Plan & Run-of-Show
prompt: Produce a complete operational event plan and day-of run-of-show for a 1-day, 250-attendee Civic Tech Summit at a downtown civic center. Cover objectives and venue layout, full-day schedule (keynote, 2 parallel tracks, lunch, workshops, closing reception), itemized budget under $38,000 with a 10% contingency reserve, vendor/AV logistics, staffing roles, and day-of risk contingencies.
materials:
Venue & Vendor Sheet:
1. Civic Center Rental: Main Hall (300 seats, $9,500) + 3 Breakout Rooms (60 seats each, $4,500 total). ADA elevator access on East Wing only.
2. Catering Quote: Continental breakfast + plated lunch + afternoon coffee = $46/person ($11,500 for 250); vegetarian/vegan/gluten-free menus required 10 days prior.
3. AV Vendor: Main stage sound/projection + 3 room kits = $6,200; live captioning + livestream package adds $3,800.
4. Staffing & Ops: 12 volunteers, 2 paid stage managers ($1,400), signage/badges ($2,100), speaker travel stipends ($2,400).
5. Keynote speaker (City CTO) has a hard departure at 10:30 AM.
mid_task_requirement: Mid-task sponsor update (inject at ~50% progress): Budget is cut from $38,000 to $31,000 AND we must add a live captioned hybrid stream for 200 remote attendees (ADA compliance). Keep the confirmed morning Keynote schedule (ending before 10:30 AM) untouched.
rubric_criteria: Feasible, conflict-free full-day schedule honoring 10:30 AM keynote constraint (0-2 pts)
Itemized budget mathematically reconciled under revised $31,000 cap with contingency (0-2 pts)
Complete hybrid livestream & ADA live-captioning operational plan (0-2 pts)
Concrete venue routing, dietary, staffing, and incident contingency coverage (0-2 pts)
Actionability and clarity for a day-of operations team (0-2 pts)

title: B2B SaaS Q3 Retention & Churn Data-Analysis Report
prompt: Analyze the provided Q1-Q3 SaaS cohort dataset and write an executive data-analysis report diagnosing the Q3 churn spike. Audit metric definitions and data caveats, quantify segment differences (SMB, Mid-Market, Enterprise), evaluate competing root-cause hypotheses (Day-14 activation drop vs. P1 support load vs. July pricing change), and recommend 3 prioritized retention experiments with projected ARR impact and A/B test guardrails.
materials:
Embedded Cohort Summary Table (Q1 -> Q2 -> Q3):
- SMB ($180 ARPA, 2,400 accts): Monthly logo churn 3.0% -> 3.1% -> 5.4%; Day-14 activation 68% -> 66% -> 49% (new self-serve wizard launched Jul 4); Avg P1 tickets/100 accts 2.1 -> 2.3 -> 2.6.
- Mid-Market ($1,400 ARPA, 420 accts): Monthly logo churn 1.4% -> 1.5% -> 2.1%; Day-14 activation 79% -> 78% -> 76%; Avg P1 tickets/100 accts 3.0 -> 3.2 -> 6.8 (billing sync bug Jul 18 - Aug 29).
- Enterprise ($8,500 ARPA, 65 accts): Monthly logo churn 0.4% -> 0.4% -> 0.5%; Net Revenue Retention 114% -> 113% -> 112%; 18 renewals due in Q4.
- Data Caveat: July 12-15 analytics outage caused 140 SMB activation events to be logged as NULL (excluded from raw activation % unless imputed).
mid_task_requirement: Mid-task CFO request (inject at ~50% progress): Refocus the executive recommendations for tomorrow's Board meeting on protecting Q4 Mid-Market & Enterprise renewal ARR (at least $600k ARR at risk), include an explicit sensitivity note on the July 12-15 NULL analytics outage, and do NOT alter the already-verified Dataset Audit section.
rubric_criteria: Accurate quantitative synthesis of SMB, Mid-Market, and Enterprise trends (0-2 pts)
Rigorous root-cause separation (SMB onboarding wizard vs. Mid-Market billing bug) (0-2 pts)
Explicit sensitivity treatment of July 12-15 NULL analytics outage & caveats (0-2 pts)
Board-focused Q4 Mid-Market/Enterprise ARR protection plan & experiments (0-2 pts)
Coherence, executive polish, and preserved Dataset Audit consistency (0-2 pts)
